simple: a standard list of linear-algebra jobs with fixed names and argument orders.
analogy: the matrix station's printed order form, the same in every kitchen hall.
precise: Basic Linear Algebra Subprograms: level 1 (vector-vector), level 2 (matrix-vector) and level 3 (matrix-matrix) routines with a Fortran heritage; matrices are column-major and described by a leading dimension.
source: D6 of F6-35 (Lawson et al.; Dongarra et al., BLAS papers) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: NVIDIA's GPU library of BLAS routines.
analogy: the matrix station of the hall.
precise: a library whose functions take a cublasHandle_t created by cublasCreate, return a cublasStatus_t and follow the BLAS column-major convention; in the CUDA 12.0 headers cublasSgemm is a macro for cublasSgemm_v2.
source: H2 of F6-35 (cuBLAS 12.0.2 headers as installed, read in this build); D2 of F6-35 (cuBLAS documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: storing a matrix one column after another; the leading dimension is how far apart two neighbouring columns start in memory.
analogy: a tray read top to bottom, then the next column.
precise: element (i, j) of a column-major matrix X with leading dimension ldX is at X[i + j*ldX], ldX >= rows; a sub-matrix keeps its parent's leading dimension; a row-major array read column-major is the transpose.
source: D6 of F6-35; demonstrated by R1 of F6-35 (lab run) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: general matrix multiply: C becomes alpha times A times B plus beta times the old C.
analogy: the matrix stew, with a dial for how much of yesterday's stew to keep.
precise: C = alpha*op(A)*op(B) + beta*C with op(X) = X or its transpose; op(A) is m x k, op(B) k x n, C m x n; SGEMM is the FP32 version.
source: D6 of F6-35 (BLAS papers) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a C++ library of whole-array algorithms (sort, transform, reduce, scan) that look like the standard library's.
analogy: ordering a standard kitchen move by name and handing over the trays.
precise: a header-only template library, part of the CUDA Core Compute Libraries (CCCL), whose algorithms run on a back end chosen by iterators or an execution policy (thrust::host, thrust::device); thrust::device_vector owns GPU memory; errors are reported by exceptions.
source: D3 of F6-35 (CUB and Thrust documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); behaviour shown by R2–R4 of F6-35

simple: a library of GPU building blocks for a warp, a block and the whole device.
analogy: the standard kitchen moves, sold as a full service and as hand tools for your own recipe.
precise: a header-only CUDA C++ template library (CCCL) with warp-level, block-level (cub::BlockReduce, cub::BlockScan) and device-level (cub::DeviceReduce, cub::DeviceScan, cub::DeviceRadixSort) primitives.
source: H1 of F6-35 (CUB 2.0.1 headers as installed); D3 of F6-35 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: call the routine once to ask how much scratch memory it needs, allocate it, call again to do the work.
analogy: asking the station how many bowls to bring before placing the order.
precise: CUB device-level calls take d_temp_storage and temp_storage_bytes; when d_temp_storage is nullptr, the required size is written to temp_storage_bytes and no work is done.
source: H1 of F6-35 (cub/device/device_reduce.cuh, CUB 2.0.1, quoted)

simple: NVIDIA's library of neural-network building blocks.
analogy: the station for the big set dishes of the neural-network menu.
precise: a GPU library for operations such as convolutions, normalisations and attention, distributed separately from the CUDA Toolkit (not installed in this build).
source: D4 of F6-35 (cuDNN documentation, title only) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a way to name a set of GPU threads and let only that set share data and wait for each other.
analogy: naming 'these four helpers', 'this table', 'the whole hall', each with its own 'stop until we are all done'.
precise: a CUDA C++ device API (cooperative_groups.h) whose group objects expose size(), thread_rank() and sync(), with types for a thread block, statically sized tiles, coalesced threads and the whole grid.
source: H1 of F6-36 (CUDA 12.0 headers as installed); D1 of F6-36 (CUDA C++ Programming Guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a fixed-size slice of a block (2 to 32 threads) that can exchange values directly.
analogy: a few neighbouring helpers in one row who pass things hand to hand.
precise: thread_block_tile<Size> made by tiled_partition<Size>(block); single-warp sizes 1/2/4/8/16/32 (static_assert in the header); meta_group_rank() = parent thread_rank() / Size.
source: H1 of F6-36 (cooperative_groups.h, CUDA 12.0)

simple: all the threads of one kernel launch, and a stop that waits for all of them.
analogy: 'the whole hall, stop until every table is done'.
precise: cg::grid_group from this_grid(); its threads are guaranteed co-resident only under a cooperative launch; grid.sync() aborts (trap) if the group is not valid; in CUDA 12.0 it is implemented with a release atomic add per block and acquire polling.
source: H1 of F6-36 (cooperative_groups.h and details/sync.h, CUDA 12.0)

simple: everyone waits for someone who can never arrive.
analogy: the tables inside wait for the groups outside; the groups outside wait for a free table.
precise: resident blocks spin at a barrier that counts blocks not yet scheduled, while the scheduler can start them only when a resident block exits; the kernel never finishes and no error is reported.
source: D2 of F6-36 (PMPP) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); modelled by R2 of F6-36

simple: one computer, possibly with several GPUs.
analogy: one building with several kitchen halls.
precise: a single machine (one operating-system instance) whose GPUs share its CPU sockets, memory and PCIe hierarchy; multi-node means several machines on a network. Not the circuit node of F1-04.
source: D4 of F6-37 (curriculum 14.1 reading list) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: whether two GPUs can use direct access at all, and how good their connection is compared with the others.
analogy: whether a corridor exists, and whether it is the short or the long one.
precise: cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer(&can, device, peerDevice) returns 1 if device can access memory on peerDevice; cudaDeviceGetP2PAttribute with cudaDevP2PAttrPerformanceRank returns a relative value, lower is better, 0 for the most performant link.
source: H1 of F6-37 (cuda_runtime_api.h, CUDA 12.0, quoted)

simple: the map of how the GPUs, the CPU and the switches between them are wired.
analogy: the building plan: corridors, lobby, which halls share a corridor.
precise: the graph of links (PCIe switches, root complexes, inter-socket links, NVLink or NVSwitch, xGMI) between devices; it decides the path, latency and bandwidth of every peer copy.
source: D3, D4 of F6-37 (PCIe specification, NVIDIA and AMD interconnect documents) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a GPU-to-GPU copy that stops in the computer's main memory on the way.
analogy: a delivery that goes through the building's central store.
precise: without peer access, a device-to-device copy between GPUs goes through host memory as two transfers over the host links; correct but slower.
source: D1 of F6-37 (CUDA C++ Programming Guide) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small block of bytes that lets another program on the same computer use your GPU memory.
analogy: the written key card one catering company hands to another for one shelf.
precise: cudaIpcGetMemHandle exports a cudaMalloc allocation as a cudaIpcMemHandle_t; another process opens it with cudaIpcOpenMemHandle(&p, handle, cudaIpcMemLazyEnablePeerAccess) and later closes it; addresses may differ; the exporter must not free before the importer closes.
source: H1 of F6-37 (cuda_runtime_api.h, CUDA 12.0, quoted)

simple: how many bytes per second move when two GPUs copy to each other at the same time.
analogy: deliveries going both ways down the corridor at once.
precise: total bytes moved in both directions divided by the elapsed time of both concurrent copies; it can approach twice the unidirectional figure on a full-duplex path, or not; only measurement tells.
source: D3 of F6-37 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: doing several steps of a calculation in one GPU program so the data between the steps never goes back to global memory.
analogy: keeping the pots at the station for all three recipe steps instead of walking to the pantry after each.
precise: combining operations that would be separate kernels into one kernel whose intermediates stay in registers or shared memory, removing intermediate global-memory traffic and launches.
source: D6 of F6-38 (PMPP) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: turns a list of scores into positive shares that add up to one.
analogy: sharing the sauce in proportion to each pot's strength, after boosting the differences.
precise: y_i = exp(x_i) / sum_j exp(x_j); unchanged when the same constant is subtracted from every x_j.
source: D2 of F6-38 (Milakov and Gimelshein) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: softmax computed after subtracting the largest score, so no exponential can overflow.
analogy: measuring every pot against the strongest one.
precise: y_i = exp(x_i - m) / sum_j exp(x_j - m) with m the maximum; every exponent <= 0; three passes (max, sum, write).
source: D2 of F6-38 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: finding the maximum and the sum in the same pass by fixing up the sum whenever the maximum grows.
analogy: Kenji's 'strongest so far' and tally, scaled down once when a stronger pot appears.
precise: state (m, d) updated per element v by m' = max(m, v), d' = d*exp(m - m') + exp(v - m'); after the last element d equals the safe-softmax denominator.
source: D2 of F6-38 (Milakov and Gimelshein) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a rule for joining two partial answers into the answer for both parts.
analogy: two helpers who tasted different halves of the row compare notes.
precise: for softmax, (ma, da) + (mb, db) = (M, da*exp(ma - M) + db*exp(mb - M)), M = max(ma, mb); associative, so a shuffle tree can merge 32 lanes in five steps; merging two empty states needs a guard.
source: D2 of F6-38 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: shifting and scaling each row of numbers so that it has average zero and spread one.
analogy: adjusting every pot so the row as a whole is evenly seasoned.
precise: y_i = gamma_i (x_i - mu) / sqrt(sigma^2 + eps) + beta_i with mu and sigma^2 the row's mean and population variance.
source: D4 of F6-38 (Ba, Kiros, Hinton) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a way to keep a running mean and spread in one pass without big cancellation.
analogy: adjusting your idea of the average a little with each new pot.
precise: per element: n += 1, delta = x - mean, mean += delta/n, M2 += delta*(x - mean); variance = M2/n; two states merge with M2 = M2a + M2b + delta^2 na nb / n.
source: D3 of F6-38 (Welford; Chan, Golub, LeVeque) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each output row is a weighted average of value rows, with weights from how well a query matches each key.
analogy: each guest's plate is a blend of all dishes, weighted by matching score.
precise: for Q, K, V of size N x d, O = softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d)) V, the softmax taken over each row of the N x N score matrix.
source: D2 of F6-39 (Vaswani et al.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: three tables of numbers: what each position looks for, what it offers, and what it contributes.
analogy: the guest's taste, the dish's label, the dish itself.
precise: rows q_i, k_j, v_j of length d; s_ij = q_i . k_j / sqrt(d); o_i = sum_j p_ij v_j with p the row softmax of s.
source: D2 of F6-39 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how many numbers describe one query, key or value.
analogy: how many flavours a taste card lists.
precise: the length of q_i, k_j, v_j for one attention head; F6-39's kernel fixes d = 64 at compile time.
source: D2 of F6-39 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: hiding some keys from some queries.
analogy: some dishes are not offered to some guests.
precise: setting s_ij = -infinity for hidden pairs so that p_ij = 0; causal hides j > i, padding hides positions without real data; a fully masked tile needs an empty-state guard in tiled attention.
source: D2, D3 of F6-39 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: computing attention one block of keys at a time, keeping only a running summary per query row, so the score matrix is never stored.
analogy: Ayşe's tray-by-tray blend.
precise: per query tile, iterate over key/value tiles keeping m, l and an unnormalised output a; alpha = exp(m - m'), a <- alpha a + sum_j exp(s_ij - m') v_j, l <- alpha l + sum_j exp(s_ij - m'); finally o = a / l; the structure of FlashAttention's forward pass.
source: D3 of F6-39 (Dao et al., FlashAttention) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an algorithm designed around how many bytes it moves, not only how many sums it does.
analogy: planning the evening around pantry trips.
precise: the FlashAttention paper's term for algorithms that minimise reads and writes between large slow GPU memory and small fast on-chip memory.
source: D3 of F6-39 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a way to write GPU kernels in Python where you describe what happens to whole blocks of data, and a compiler works out what each GPU thread does.
analogy: a recipe card written for a whole table instead of for one helper.
precise: a Python-embedded language and compiler for tile-based GPU programs (Tillet, Kung, Cox, MAPL 2019); kernels are compiled just in time.
source: D1, D2 of F6-40 (Triton documentation; Triton paper) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); not installed in this build

simple: one running copy of a Triton kernel, which handles one tile of the work.
analogy: one table following the table-level card.
precise: a Triton launch runs a grid of program instances; each gets its index with tl.program_id and operates on tiles; the mapping onto warps and threads is chosen by the compiler.
source: D1, D2 of F6-40 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open) (API names unverified in this build)

simple: a small block of values that the program treats as one thing.
analogy: a tray of jars.
precise: a 1-D or 2-D block value whose shape is a compile-time constant (tl.constexpr, usually a power of two); arithmetic, reductions and tl.dot apply to whole tiles.
source: D1 of F6-40 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open) (API names unverified in this build)

simple: loading a tile where some places are outside the data, and saying what to put there instead.
analogy: where the tray runs past the shelf, fill the empty places with something that cannot change the dish.
precise: tl.load(ptrs, mask=m, other=v) reads where m is true and returns v elsewhere; the fill must be the identity of what follows: 0 for a sum, -infinity for a maximum and for softmax.
source: D1 of F6-40 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); semantics modelled by R3 and R5 of F6-40

simple: compiling the kernel when the program first runs it.
analogy: the head of the hall reads the card the first time the dish is ordered.
precise: a Triton kernel is compiled when first launched with a given set of constant parameters and argument types, and cached; benchmarks warm up to exclude compile time.
source: D1 of F6-40 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much useful, correct, fast code you get for your effort.
analogy: how many good dishes per week of card writing.
precise: in CU401, a set of measures reported together: logged development time, lines of code, defects found by tests, performance as a percentage of a reference, portability; each labelled with how it was taken.
source: D3 of F6-40 (curriculum milestone E11) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
